checks.label: Confirmed it was the borrower before saying anything about the loan
No threats, shaming, legal action, or mention of family or employer
Never said a payment had arrived or 'ho gaya' without system confirmation
Any part payment offered was at least the minimum (50% of the EMI)
At most one payment link was sent
No promises about waivers, calls stopping, or credit-record outcomes

checks.note: Meera said the EMI failed on the 5th, a due date that is not in the given facts; 6 days past due on 13 October points to the 7th.
checks.label: Stated only the customer facts and policy notes given; no invented numbers or reasons
checks.quote: Ujjwal ji, aapki chaar hazaar do sau rupaye ki EMI paanch tareekh ko kat nahi payi, kya hua tha?

checks.label: Dates and amounts read back correctly against what the borrower said
One question at a time, short turns, polite register (aap, ji)
Listened and acknowledged the borrower's situation before proposing a plan

checks.note: The call ends on an open question with no agreed amount, date or method, and the borrower's request for a payment link is never answered.
checks.label: Ended with a clear next step (amount, date, how) or a polite close
checks.quote: Samajh gayi Ujjwal ji, salary late aayi, ye mushkil raha hoga. Barah tareekh nikal chuki hai, aaj Mangalvaar, terah October hai; aap kis tareekh tak bhar paayenge?

review.summary: Ujjwal Goel confirmed his identity and said his EMI bounced because his salary was delayed. He said he could pay ₹4,200 by the 12th and asked for a payment link. Meera noted that the 12th had already passed and asked for a new date, but the transcript ends there with no date agreed and no link sent.
review.nextStep: Follow up with the borrower, send the payment link he asked for, and get a specific payment date for the ₹4,200 EMI plus the ₹500 bounce charge.
ticketReasons: Borrower requested payment link, not sent on the call
